data.body_html:
August 2045 in Marbella means long sunny days, warm 26°C seas, and a lively buzz around Puerto Banús. For a yacht charter, it's peak season — which brings both incredible conditions and the need for smart planning. This guide gives you the exact weather picture, what to expect on the water, and practical tips to make the most of your day, whether you're on a 2-hour spin or a full-day cruise.

August 2045 Weather Outlook for Marbella

Expect daily highs around 31°C, with overnight lows near 22°C. Sea surface temperature averages 26°C — warm enough for swimming all day. Rain is rare (less than 5% of days), so you can plan with confidence. The sun rises at 07:30 and sets at 21:15, giving you over 13 hours of daylight.

Winds are typically light: 0-4 knots in the morning, building to 8-12 knots by mid-afternoon. This creates a gentle sea breeze that keeps things comfortable. Swell heights average 0.3-0.6m, though the afternoon Levante can produce a short chop of 0.5-1m beyond Cabopino.

Best Times of Day for Your Charter

Morning charters (10:00-14:00) offer the calmest seas and cooler temperatures. Midday is perfect for swimming and sunbathing. Late afternoon (16:00-20:00) brings a lively breeze and golden light for photos. Sunset charters (19:00-21:15) are magical but book fast — we recommend the 4-hour slot from 16:00.

If you're prone to heat, choose a morning slot on the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — it's a Tier A boat at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks.

What to Wear and Pack for August

Light layers are key: a swimsuit, a rash guard or linen shirt for sun protection, and a light windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. Bring a hat, polarized sunglasses, and reef-safe sunscreen (SPF 50+). Evening returns can feel cooler, so a light jumper is wise. Non-slip boat shoes are recommended; no heels or dark-soled shoes.

Don't forget a towel, a small bag for valuables (waterproof is best), and a camera. Our boats have shaded flybridges and air-conditioned cabins, so you can always escape the heat.

Sea Conditions and Navigation Tips

August seas are generally calm, but the afternoon Levante can create a short chop. Our skippers know the local waters intimately. They'll adjust your route to sheltered coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés if needed. Heading west to Estepona often yields smoother water, while east towards Cabopino offers more anchorages.

For a longer cruise, consider the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) — it's a Tier B boat at €4,719 for 4 hours, and includes a free jet ski, perfect for exploring coves.

Booking Strategy for Peak Season

August 2045 will see high demand, especially for weekends and the first two weeks. Book 3-4 weeks ahead for weekends; midweek dates are more flexible but still sell out 10-14 days prior. The Mangusta 80 (Grey) and Ferretti 94 are particularly popular for group celebrations.

For last-minute plans, Tier A boats like the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) are often available at €749 for 2 hours. Check our fleet page for the full list and current availability.

What's Included in Every Charter

All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs — the price you see is the price you pay. For Tier A boats, the 2-hour rate is €749; the 8-hour rate is €2,299. For Tier B (Mangusta 80), the minimum is 4 hours at €4,719, with the jet ski included free.

Other boats (e.g., Azimut 58 Flybridge, Pershing 46) are priced on request via WhatsApp — just ask for a custom quote.

Local Highlights for Your August Cruise

From Puerto Banús, you can head to the iconic Marbella Marina for a lunch stop, or cruise along the Golden Mile to see the villas. Further east, Cabopino offers a quieter anchorage, while west to Estepona gives you a taste of old-town charm. Sotogrande, about 40 minutes by sea, is worth the trip for its marina and beach clubs.

For a full-day adventure, consider the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) — it's a spacious platform for groups, with plenty of shade and comfort.

Beat the Heat: On-Board Comfort

All our yachts have shaded flybridges or bimini tops, plus air-conditioned cabins. We provide chilled drinks and ice throughout the day. For extra comfort, bring a towel and a small cooler bag for personal items. If you're on a Tier B boat, the jet ski adds a fun way to cool off — just remember to wear a life jacket.

Our skippers are happy to adjust the pace to your preference, whether you want a fast cruise or a leisurely drift.
